svg.text: Deployment — A Careful Script With No Rollback
Smart Credit Solution Enterprises Admin Portal
deploy.bat → deploy.ps1 — the deployment pipeline, step by step
1. Check SSH connectivity
abort if VPN/server unreachable
2. git fetch + detached worktree
clean build from origin/master, not local state
3. mvnw clean install -DskipTests
tests never gate a deployment
4. scp WAR to server (/tmp)
dedicated key, batch mode, no password fallback
— remote, over SSH, as a single base64-encoded bash script —
5. sudo -n mkdir backups; cp current WAR → timestamped backup file
6. shutdown.sh, then poll up to 150s for Tomcat to actually stop
aborts deployment (exit 1) if Tomcat is still running — avoids a double instance
7. sudo -n rm -f DEPLOY_WAR ; sudo -n rm -rf EXPLODED_DIR
the OLD, currently-working WAR is deleted HERE — before the new one is confirmed to work
only copy of the working version left is the untouched backup file from step 5
8. mv new WAR into place; chmod 664; startup.sh
9. Confirm success by: process count > 0, AND exploded WAR directory appears within 60s
no HTTP health check — a running process with an exploded WAR can still have a Spring context that failed to start
⚠ CRITICAL — the backup from step 5 is never automatically restored
Both failure exits — "Tomcat failed to start" and "Application deployment folder was not created" — do the same thing:
tail -n 100 catalina.out ; exit 1
Neither branch copies $BACKUP_FILE back to $DEPLOY_WAR or restarts Tomcat with the known-good version.
A failed deployment leaves the site down, with the old working WAR sitting only in a backup file —
recovery requires someone to SSH in and restore it by hand.
Other findings
No CI/CD pipeline exists
Confirmed by absence: no .github/workflows,
no pipeline YAML anywhere in the repo.
Deployment is fully manual — a developer
runs deploy.bat locally, requiring VPN
access and a locally-held SSH key.
Passwordless sudo on the deploy account
Every remote file operation uses sudo -n
(non-interactive). A leaked deploy SSH key
grants passwordless root-level file access
on the production Tomcat server — no
second factor stands between key and shell.
Single hardcoded target, no env selection
deploy-config.ps1 hardcodes one host
(10.1.3.5) and one Tomcat path. This script
has no visibility into which Spring profile
(uat/prod, Module 1) the deployed WAR
actually runs under on that server.
.gitignore confirms, firsthand, that Module 1's finding is real
No application*.properties pattern is excluded anywhere in .gitignore — the plaintext DB passwords, vendor API keys, and
AES base secret documented in Module 1 are genuinely committed to source control, not just locally present and untracked.
By contrast: this is a carefully engineered script in several real respects
• Reproducible builds — a detached git worktree from origin/master, not whatever happens to be on the local disk
• Dedicated SSH key, IdentitiesOnly + BatchMode (no interactive password fallback), sane connection timeouts
• Waits for Tomcat to actually stop before touching files, and aborts outright rather than risking a double-instance
• Waits for the exploded WAR directory post-restart, and tails the last 100 log lines on any failure for diagnostics
• Cleans up the temporary git worktree on both the success and failure paths
• Base64-encodes the remote bash script specifically to avoid CRLF/line-ending corruption over SSH — a real, subtle problem, deliberately solved
Sound engineering, by contrast
Standard step / minor finding
Flagged risk
Critical — confirmed operational gap
Generated from source review — Smart Credit Solution Enterprises Admin Portal — module 14 of the architecture documentation set
